findings.evidence: `Index.lean:130`: `| .C rank q => 3 ≤ rank ∧ q.p ≠ 2`; grep for `characteristic_ne_two` / `Odd` over `code/TauCeti` returns no such lemma for any Lie index.
findings.fix: Add `theorem characteristic_ne_two (d : TypeCLieIndex) : d.1.characteristic ≠ 2` (or `Odd d.1.characteristic`) next to `three_le_rank`, proved the same way from `(inStandardRange_iff _).mp ... |>.2`.
findings.issue: Only half of the type-C standard range is exposed. `three_le_rank` is proved, but the odd-characteristic half of `InStandardRange` for `.C` (`q.p ≠ 2`) has no lemma, although both the module docstring (line 18) and the `TypeCLieIndex` docstring (line 85) advertise it ("its characteristic is odd"), and it is the condition that excludes the `C_r(2^e) = B_r(2^e)` overlap.

findings.evidence: Lines 98-108, 126-132, 136-142 each open with `obtain ⟨⟨d, _⟩, hC⟩ := d; change d.IsTypeC at hC; cases d <;> try contradiction`.
findings.fix: Expose an elimination lemma, e.g. `theorem exists_eq_ofC (d : TypeCLieIndex) : ∃ r q h, d = ofC r q h` (or `∃ r q, d.1.1 = .C r q`), and use it for the three in-file proofs. Also add the `isTypeC_iff` characterization that `Index.lean` gives every other selector (`inStandardRange_iff`, `usesHalfFrobenius_iff`, `isDuplicateRepresentative_iff`).
findings.issue: `ofC` is the introduction form but there is no elimination principle for `TypeCLieIndex`, so every consumer that must see the underlying `.C rank q` has to repeat the subtype-destructuring dance. The file itself repeats it three times (`three_le_rank` lines 99-103, `toGraphTwistedIndex` lines 127-132, `diagramPerm_eq_one` lines 137-140), each with a `change d.IsTypeC at hC` workaround.

findings.evidence: `StandardCarrier/RootDatum.lean:78-82` states the Bourbaki identification at `(C (n + 1)).simplyConnectedRootDatum`; the new file never relates `d.1.dynkinType` to `DynkinType.C (d.carrierParameter + 1)`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem dynkinType_eq (d : TypeCLieIndex) : d.1.dynkinType = .C d.1.rank` (hence `.C (d.carrierParameter + 1)`), which is what lets `SpStd.rootGeneratorWeight_inl_eq_root_simpleIndex` be applied at a CFSG index.
findings.issue: The reindexing is only justified numerically (`carrierParameter + 1 = d.1.rank`); nothing exposes that the index's Dynkin type is the carrier's type, so a consumer cannot connect `simpleRootSubgroup i` to the pinned datum without redoing the constructor case split.

findings.evidence: TypeC.lean:167-170 docstring: "because `steinberg` is transparent, `TauCeti.SpStd.coe_frobenius_apply` already supplies the canonical simp normal form in terms of the characteristic and field exponent"; Index.lean:472 `fieldOrder_eq_characteristic_pow` carries no attribute.
findings.fix: Make `steinberg` a `def` (keeping `AmbientGroup` reducible) so the CFSG-level lemmas own the normal form, and mark `coe_steinberg_apply` `@[simp]`; restate any SpStd Frobenius lemma a consumer needs. If transparency is deliberate instead, drop `coe_steinberg_apply` and state the pinned equations in the `characteristic ^ fieldExponent` spelling — one spelling, not two.
findings.issue: `steinberg` is a reducible `abbrev`, so `SpStd.coe_frobenius_apply` (`@[simp]`, Frobenius.lean:147) fires through it and normalizes coefficients to `... ^ d.1.characteristic ^ d.1.fieldExponent`, while `steinberg_simpleRootSubgroup` (`@[simp]`) produces the `d.1.fieldOrder` spelling and no simp lemma reconciles the two (`fieldOrder_eq_characteristic_pow` is not `@[simp]`). `coe_steinberg_apply` is consequently unreachable by `simp`, as its own docstring concedes.

findings.evidence: Line 194: `simp only [diagramPerm_eq_one, Equiv.Perm.coe_one, id_eq]` is the first proof step, normalizing away the RHS's own `diagramPerm` application.
findings.fix: State the simp lemma with `d.simpleRootSubgroup i (...)` on the right; if the uniform `γ ∘ Frob_q` shape is wanted for the L1 table, keep it as a separate non-simp restatement.
findings.issue: `steinberg_simpleRootSubgroup` is `@[simp]` but its RHS is not simp-normal: it contains `d.toGraphTwistedIndex.diagramPerm i`, which the file's own `@[simp] diagramPerm_eq_one` (line 135) immediately rewrites to `i` — the proof's first step is exactly that rewrite.

summary: The type-C surface is missing the elimination/characteristic lemmas its own docstrings advertise (odd characteristic, destructuring a type-C index, the Dynkin-type bridge to the carrier), and the `steinberg` abbrev leaves two competing spellings of `q` with the CFSG-level `coe_steinberg_apply` unreachable by `simp`.
